"Erstelle ein mobiles Fantasy-MMORPG namens AETHERIA mit düsterer Fantasy-Welt, schöner Grafik und Touch-Steuerung.

Klassen @COMMENT_BODY@ Charaktere: Engel oder Dämon als Fraktion, männlich oder weiblich. Klassen: Krieger, Magier und Assassine mit eigenen Waffen, Rüstungen und Fähigkeiten. Charaktername, Frisuren, Haarfarben, Augenfarben und Startoutfits.

Ausrüstung: 9 Ausrüstungsslots, Klassen- und Levelanforderungen. Items haben die Stufen T3, T2 und T1 sowie verschiedene Seltenheiten.

Fusion: 4 identische Items ergeben die nächste Stufe: T3 → T2 → T1 → nächste Seltenheit T3. Kein zufälliges Zerstören. 4 Legendary = Mythic, 4 Mythic = Divine.

Drops: Common 60%, Grey 25%, Green 10%, Blue 5%. Monster droppen immer T3. Purple und höher droppen nicht direkt. Legendary wird gecraftet. Bosssteine haben bis zu 3 Boni. Krit-Chance maximal 50%.

Welt: 8 große Gebiete: Greendale, Ironcrag, Venomwood, Mistgrave, Frostpeak, Sunscorch Desert, Ashen Dominion und Tower of Eternity. Mit Monstern, Elitegegnern, Bossen und Quests. Die ersten 2 Gebiete haben NPCs, spätere nur Rückkehr-Teleporter.

Systeme: Level, XP, Gold, Gems, Quests, Inventar, Lager, Händler, Spielerhandel, Sammeln, Crafting, Schmied und Mounts. Keine Reparaturen.

Flügel: Nur über Quests oder Shop, keine Drops, nicht handelbar oder fusionierbar.

Shop: Kostüme, Frisuren, Mounts, Pets, Waffeneffekte, Flügel und Gems. Free-to-play, Gems auch erspielbar.

Einstellungen: Sprachwahl zwischen Deutsch und Englisch. Das gesamte Spiel muss vollständig übersetzbar sein, einschließlich Menüs, Einstellungen, Quests, Items, NPC-Dialogen, Systemmeldungen und Buttons. Die gewählte Sprache muss gespeichert bleiben und nach einem Neustart erhalten bleiben.

Erstelle ein echtes spielbares Android-Mobilegame mit modularer Struktur, schöner UI, großen Maps und Ladeübergängen. Keine PC-Version. Multiplayer soll später mit echten Servern erweiterbar sein, nicht simuliert werden.

---

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.

---
name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}"
on:
  issues:
    types:
      - opened
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        required: true
        type: string
        description: Existing issue to run
permissions: {}
concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false
jobs:
  prepare:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      id-token: write
      contents: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    outputs:
      approved: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.approved }}
      issue_number: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ steps.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    steps:
      - name: Authenticate status callbacks
        continue-on-error: true
        shell: bash
        env:
          ISSUE_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
          OMGITHUB_ORIGIN: ${{ vars.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN || 'https://omgithub.com' }}
        run: |
          /usr/bin/time -p node --input-type=module <<'NODE'
          import { appendFileSync } from 'node:fs';
          const env = process.env;
          const origin = env.OMGITHUB_ORIGIN.replace(/\/$/, '');
          const url = new URL(env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL);
          url.searchParams.set('audience', origin);
          async function json(url, options) {
            const response = await fetch(url, { ...options, signal: AbortSignal.timeout(15000) });
            if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`Callback authentication HTTP ${response.status}`);
            return response.json();
          }
          for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt++) {
            try {
              const identity = await json(url, { headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${env.ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN}` } });
              const { token } = await json(`${origin}/api/github/${env.GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${env.ISSUE_NUMBER}/callback-token`, {
                method: 'POST', headers: { authorization: `Bearer ${identity.value}`, 'content-type': 'application/json' },
                body: JSON.stringify({ run: env.GITHUB_RUN_ID, attempt: Number(env.GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT) })
              });
              console.log(`::add-mask::${token}`);

export function getLang() { return lang; }

export function setLang(next) {
  if (next !== 'de' && next !== 'en') return;
  lang = next;
  document.documentElement.lang = next;
  try { document.documentElement.dataset.lang = next; } catch {}
}

export function t(key, vars) {
  let str = DICT[lang]?.[key] ?? DICT.en?.[key] ?? DICT.de?.[key] ?? key;
  if (vars) {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(vars)) str = str.replaceAll(`{${k}}`, String(v));
  }
  return str;
}

export function tx(value) {
  if (value == null) return '';
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value;
  return value[lang] ?? value.en ?? value.de ?? '';
}

export function hasKey(key) {
  return Boolean(DICT[lang]?.[key] || DICT.en?.[key]);
}

export function translationStats() {
  const de = Object.keys(DICT.de).length;
  const en = Object.keys(DICT.en).length;
  const missingEn = Object.keys(DICT.de).filter((k) => !DICT.en[k]);
  const missingDe = Object.keys(DICT.en).filter((k) => !DICT.de[k]);
  return { de, en, missingEn, missingDe };
}

## Objective
- Create a complete, playable, mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG named AETHERIA with touch controls, eight large regions, character progression, inventory/crafting systems, localization, and later multiplayer extensibility.

## Requirements
- Classes: Warrior, Mage, Assassin; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- 9 equipment slots, class/level requirements, T3/T2/T1 tiers, and rarity progression.
- Equipment fusion: 4 identical items advance tier/rarity; 4 Legendary → Mythic and 4 Mythic → Divine; no destruction.
- Monster drops: Common 60%, Grey 25%, Green 10%, Blue 5%; monsters always drop T3; Legendary and higher are crafted; boss stones support up to 3 bonuses; critical chance capped at 50%.
- Eight zones: Greendale, Ironcrag, Venomwood, Mistgrave, Frostpeak, Sunscorch Desert, Ashen Dominion, Tower of Eternity.
- Quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, forge, storage, shops, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable.
- Full German/English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android game, not PC-only; multiplayer must use a real-server-ready seam rather than simulation.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a mobile-first installable web game with an Android/Capacitor wrapper direction.
- Added procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Used browser persistence for settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression.
- Added modular source directories for core systems, data, game engine, UI, and styles.

## Work State
### Completed
- Repository foundation and mobile app shell created.
- Core responsive dark-fantasy UI styling and boot screen added.
- German/English localization core, settings persistence, and save/load system implemented.
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin class data implemented.
- Character appearance data for faction, hairstyles, hair/eye colors, and outfits added.
- Item, rarity, tier, fusion, equipment, crafting, and boss-stone data foundations implemented.
- Eight-zone world data and procedural world generation foundation implemented.
- Quest chain, NPC, shop, mount, pet, wing, and consumable data structures created.
- Procedural hero, monster, terrain, and prop artwork modules created.
- Core player progression, inventory, XP, gold, gems, quests, equipment, and reward logic started.
- Touch/world engine foundation for movement, combat, monsters, gathering, and zone travel created.

### Active
- Completing and validating the playable UI flow and all game screens.
- Verifying world rendering and gameplay loops end-to-end.

### Blocked
- No runtime verification or screenshots are confirmed in the conversation.
- Android signing/build tooling and actual backend multiplayer server implementation are not present yet.

## Next Move
1. Review all created modules for syntax/import issues and finish missing UI screen wiring.
2. Run the app, verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
3. Capture a small JPEG for visual verification and fix rendering/layout issues.
4. Add Android Capacitor packaging and the real multiplayer server/client transport seam.

## Relevant Files
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html`: Main application shell and boot screen.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/i18n.js`: Localization dictionary and runtime language switching.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/save.js`: Settings and player save persistence.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/core/game.js`: Player, progression, inventory, quests, equipment, and economy logic.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/classes.js`: Factions, classes, appearances, and class abilities.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/items.js`: Items, rarities, tiers, slots, fusion, stones, and stats.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/zones.js`: Eight-region definitions and zone properties.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/quests.js`: Quest chains and objectives.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/data/shop.js`: Shop tabs and purchasable cosmetic/shop content.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/worldgen.js`: Procedural large-zone generation and collisions.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/game/engine.js`: Main gameplay engine for movement, combat, monsters, loot, and travel.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/heroArt.js`: Procedural hero character rendering.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/ui/icons.js`: Shared SVG icon set.
- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/styles/base.css`: Global/mobile visual system.

## Important Context
- The implementation is an installable mobile web/PWA foundation with a planned Capacitor Android wrapper, not a completed signed APK.
- Multiplayer is deliberately not implemented as simulated content; it needs a future real-server transport integration.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a complete playable, mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep the implementation installable on Android and ready for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server-ready seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Implement as a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the app shell, responsive dark-fantasy styling, localization, persistence, class/character data, items, zones, quests, shops, procedural art, and initial gameplay engine.
- Added `src/core/audio.js` for self-contained procedural audio.
- Added `src/net/tradeClient.js` as a WebSocket transport client seam.
- Added shared UI and screen styles in `src/styles/ui.css` and `src/styles/screens.css`.
- Updated `src/game/engine.js` to localize zone names and equipment names.

### Active
- Review and finish UI screen wiring and verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Check recent audio, multiplayer, styling, and localization changes for integration and syntax issues.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current repository and validate syntax/imports, especially recent additions and the failed final write attempt.
2. Run the app and verify core gameplay flows in a browser; fix visible or functional issues.
3. Capture a small JPEG for visual verification.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Main application shell and boot flow.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, equipment, and economy logic.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `src/core/save.js`: Settings and player-save persistence.
- `src/core/audio.js`: Procedural WebAudio effects and music.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/data/classes.js`: Factions, classes, appearances, and abilities.
- `src/data/items.js`: Equipment, rarities, tiers, fusion, stones, and stats.
- `src/data/zones.js`: Eight-region definitions.
- `src/data/quests.js`: Quest chains and objectives.
- `src/game/worldgen.js`: Procedural world generation and collisions.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, monsters, loot, and travel; recently updated localization.
- `src/ui/heroArt.js`: Procedural hero rendering.
- `src/styles/ui.css`: Shared gameplay UI styling.
- `src/styles/screens.css`: Menu and screen styling.

## Important Context
- This is an installable mobile web/PWA foundation, not a completed signed APK.
- Multiplayer is not simulated; a real backend/server is still needed.
- The most recent tool action returned a write error, so inspect repository state before assuming the final intended write succeeded.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

export function getLang() { return lang; }

export function setLang(next) {
  if (next !== 'de' && next !== 'en') return;
  lang = next;
  document.documentElement.lang = next;
  try { document.documentElement.dataset.lang = next; } catch {}
}

export function t(key, vars) {
  let str = DICT[lang]?.[key] ?? DICT.en?.[key] ?? DICT.de?.[key] ?? key;
  if (vars) {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(vars)) str = str.replaceAll(`{${k}}`, String(v));
  }
  return str;
}

export function tx(value) {
  if (value == null) return '';
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value;
  return value[lang] ?? value.en ?? value.de ?? '';
}

export function hasKey(key) {
  return Boolean(DICT[lang]?.[key] || DICT.en?.[key]);
}

export function translationStats() {
  const de = Object.keys(DICT.de).length;
  const en = Object.keys(DICT.en).length;
  const missingEn = Object.keys(DICT.de).filter((k) => !DICT.en[k]);
  const missingDe = Object.keys(DICT.en).filter((k) => !DICT.de[k]);
  return { de, en, missingEn, missingDe };
}

Now design main.js. It's a huge single file potentially 1500+ lines but we can structure into src/ui/screens.js? Simpler to add main.js with everything. Need ensure functionality.

Features to implement:
- Boot sequence load settings/game, hide boot.
- Menu screen: if save, continue card, new char, settings, credits, language switch. Render hero portrait.
- Create screen: faction, class, gender, hair, colors, outfit, name, preview, start.
- Game screen: canvas, minimap, HUD with HP/resource/xp, gold/gems, zone info, quest tracker, joystick, attack button, skills with cooldown, utility buttons (potion, mount, interact, menu), menu drawer with tiles, panels.
- Panels:
  - inventory: equipment slots + bag grid + item detail modal/actions (equip/use/fuse/sell/storage)
  - character: hero art, stats, equipment
  - quests: list available/active/claimed and accept/turn in
  - world: map + zone cards travel
  - shop: tabs catalog buying, daily claim, gems
  - forge/fusion: fusion groups, boss stones reroll, salvage maybe
  - wardrobe: costumes/hair/wings/mounts/pets/fx apply
  - mounts: mount gallery call/dismiss
  - storage: bag/stash transfer
  - trade: real server UI via TradeClient
  - settings: language, audio, display, controls, reset
- Modals: item detail, confirm.
- Dialogue with NPC, accept/turn in quests, shop/forge actions.
- Toast, death, onboarding.
- Save, language switching re-render.
- Audio hooks and unlock on first pointer.
- Haptics if available.
- PWA manifest.
- Capacitor maybe later.

Need careful bugs to avoid:
- App.ui used by engine loop every frame (`App.ui?.tick(dt)`). Implement tick updating HUD DOM quickly without rebuilding. Could rebuild HUD periodically (e.g. 8fps) but update bars each frame. Simpler: build HUD once with refs; tick updates bars, cooldown, interaction, target. Use `hudRefs`. Node refs survive.
- Engine render expects canvas sized; must attach after DOM inserted with requestAnimationFrame.
- Engine's App.ui?.toast etc.
- Engine.pause when panel open? We can keep running; maybe setPaused(true) for panels except no. Actually engine paused true while panel open is nice; but ifpaused then interaction okay. Use setPaused.
- App.ui.tick is called only when engine loop runs; if not engine nothing.
- `engine.loadZone` calls `this.save()`.
- On game boot if saved player, recalc to restore stats (saved stats maybe present; newPlayer stats). loadGame returns player only; game object created via createGame.
- `engine` `App.game` etc.

Important bug: in `loadZone`, `opts.restore` checks `this.player.zoneId === zoneId` but player.zoneId was just set to zoneId line 116, so always true; x/y may be 0 if new => clamp 120, which places player near top-left instead of camp. Indeed `this.player.x = clamp(this.player.x, 120...)` with new 0 yields 120,120. That means new game starts top left. Need fix this: store prevZone/prev position before assignment, only restore if opts.restore && this.player.x && this.player.y and prior visited includes zone? We can edit engine loadZone to use previous x/y. Since player x,y set 0; use `hasPos = this.player.x > 0 && this.player.y > 0` before. `prevVisited = this.player.visited?.[zoneId]`. If restore and hasPos and prevVisited then restore, else camp. We'll patch.

Also engine `zone.palette` etc fine.

Critical engine bug: In `loadZone`, `this.zone` getter uses data already set. `generateZone` returns zone with camp. Fine. Need worldgen check npc positions and portal.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built the app shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art, and gameplay engine.
- Added procedural audio in `src/core/audio.js` and a WebSocket client seam in `src/net/tradeClient.js`.
- Updated `src/core/game.js` armor recalculation to include gear `defense` stats.
- Updated `src/game/engine.js` zone loading to capture previous location and restore it only when the destination zone was previously visited.
- Checked existing JavaScript files with `node --check`; no syntax errors were reported before the latest edits.

### Active
- Complete `src/main.js` screen/UI wiring and verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Review the recent zone-restore and armor changes for integration correctness.

### Blocked
- A large attempt to create `src/main.js` failed with `tool.input-incomplete` because the write payload exceeded the output token limit; the file’s intended content was not created.
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect current repository state and confirm `src/main.js` is absent or incomplete; create it in manageable chunks.
2. Run syntax/import checks after completing UI wiring, then launch and verify core gameplay flows in a browser.
3. Capture and inspect a small screenshot.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App shell; references `src/main.js`.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, equipment, economy, and updated armor calculation.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, loot, and updated zone restoration behavior.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `src/core/save.js`: Settings and player-save persistence.
- `src/data/items.js`: Equipment, rarities, tiers, fusion, stones, and stats.
- `src/data/zones.js`: Eight-region definitions.
- `src/data/quests.js`: Quest chains and objectives.
- `src/game/worldgen.js`: Procedural world generation and collisions.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/styles/ui.css`: Shared gameplay UI styling.
- `src/styles/screens.css`: Menu and screen styling.

## Important Context
- Repository changes are uncommitted; `git status` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, scripts, and `src/` as untracked.
- `index.html` loads `src/main.js`, but the failed write means the application entry point remains unresolved.
- The project is an installable mobile web/PWA foundation, not a completed signed APK; multiplayer still requires a real backend.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- Built app shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art, gameplay engine, procedural audio, and WebSocket client seam.
- Updated armor recalculation to include gear defense and zone loading to restore position only for previously visited zones.
- Created shared UI helpers in `src/ui/common.js` and screen modules in `src/ui/menu.js`, `src/ui/create.js`, and `src/ui/world.js`.

### Active
- Finish `src/main.js` controller and integrate the new UI modules.
- Verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Review integration of zone restoration and armor changes.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the current repository and new UI modules, then complete `src/main.js` and any missing screens or wiring.
2. Run syntax/import checks and launch the app to verify core gameplay flows.
3. Capture and inspect a small screenshot; address any runtime or UI issues.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App shell; references `src/main.js`.
- `src/main.js`: Required entry point; earlier checkpoint says missing, and recent work has not shown it being created.
- `src/ui/common.js`: Shared DOM, toast, modal, formatting, and settings helpers.
- `src/ui/menu.js`: Main menu and settings/credits UI.
- `src/ui/create.js`: Character creation UI.
- `src/ui/world.js`: HUD and world UI integration.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, equipment, economy, and armor calculation.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, loot, and zone restoration.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `src/core/save.js`: Settings and player-save persistence.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/data/items.js`: Equipment, rarities, tiers, fusion, stones, and stats.
- `src/data/zones.js`: Eight-region definitions.
- `src/styles/ui.css`: Shared gameplay UI styling.
- `src/styles/screens.css`: Menu and screen styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; earlier `git status` showed `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, scripts, and `src/` as untracked.
- The latest UI module writes were reported as completed, but their tool output was truncated; inspect files for completeness and consistency before wiring them.
- The earlier oversized `src/main.js` write failed with `tool.input-incomplete`; no subsequent history confirms successful creation.

export function getLang() { return lang; }

export function setLang(next) {
  if (next !== 'de' && next !== 'en') return;
  lang = next;
  document.documentElement.lang = next;
  try { document.documentElement.dataset.lang = next; } catch {}
}

export function t(key, vars) {
  let str = DICT[lang]?.[key] ?? DICT.en?.[key] ?? DICT.de?.[key] ?? key;
  if (vars) {
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(vars)) str = str.replaceAll(`{${k}}`, String(v));
  }
  return str;
}

export function tx(value) {
  if (value == null) return '';
  if (typeof value === 'string') return value;
  return value[lang] ?? value.en ?? value.de ?? '';
}

export function hasKey(key) {
  return Boolean(DICT[lang]?.[key] || DICT.en?.[key]);
}

export function translationStats() {
  const de = Object.keys(DICT.de).length;
  const en = Object.keys(DICT.en).length;
  const missingEn = Object.keys(DICT.de).filter((k) => !DICT.en[k]);
  const missingDe = Object.keys(DICT.en).filter((k) => !DICT.de[k]);
  return { de, en, missingEn, missingDe };
}

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Nine equipment slots, class/level requirements, tier and rarity progression, non-destructive fusion, monster drops, crafting, and boss stones.
- Eight regions, quest-driven progression, mounts, gathering, crafting, shops, storage, trading, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- App shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art/audio, gameplay engine, and WebSocket client seam exist.
- Armor recalculation includes gear defense; zone loading restores position only for previously visited zones.
- Shared UI modules and additional panel modules were written: `src/ui/common.js`, `src/ui/menu.js`, `src/ui/create.js`, `src/ui/world.js`, `src/ui/panelKit.js`, `src/ui/panels.js`, `src/ui/panels/character.js`, `src/ui/panels/quests.js`, and `src/ui/panels/shop.js`.
- Travel confirmation in `src/ui/panels/quests.js` was wired to `confirmDialog` and `panel.screen.travel`.

### Active
- Inspect and integrate new UI modules; complete missing `src/main.js` controller and verify the import graph and UI event wiring.
- Verify boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop flows.
- Review zone restoration and armor changes in gameplay context.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect the panel modules and their exports/imports, then implement or complete `src/main.js` and resolve integration issues.
2. Run syntax/import checks and launch the app to verify core gameplay flows.
3. Capture and inspect a screenshot; address runtime or UI issues.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: App shell; references `src/main.js`.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

Screen responsibilities based on usages:
- `screen.game`, `.engine`, `.hud`, `.panels`, `.settings`, `.audio`, `.tradeClient`
- `.goMenu()`, `.resetToMenu()`, `.applyLanguage()`, `.gotoCreate()`, `.continueGame()`, `.startGame(player)`, `.refreshMenu()`, `.travel(zoneId)`, `.toast(...)`, `.installPrompt?`
- `.renderMenu` cleanup handling.
- create.js expects screen.refreshMenu, screen.startGame, screen.gotoCreate.
- menu.js expects screen.continueGame, screen.gotoCreate, screen.refreshMenu, screen.installPrompt, screen.toast, screen.settings, screen.game?.player, screen.audio.
- world.js expects screen.game.player, screen.settings, screen.audio, screen.panels, screen.engine set, screen.tradeClient, screen.hud, screen.travel, goMenu, resetToMenu, settings.tutorialDone.
- panels.js expects screen.engine.setPaused, screen.audio, screen.settings, screen.applyLanguage, screen.goMenu, screen.resetToMenu, screen.travel, screen.tradeClient.state (string; note tradeClient.state is property), hud.refresh/updateQuestTracker.
- engine.js uses App.ui hooks: tick, tutorialStep, onDeath, openPanel, openDialogue, travel, toggleMenu, toast. Also App.audio, App.game, App.settings.
- game.js App has settings/game/engine/screen; engine constructor sets? No. main sets App.

- world.js `new WorldEngine(game, canvas, minimap, hud)`, attach. engine loop calls App.ui.tick. The HUD should have `tick` method; world.js class has tick. Set App.ui = hud maybe, with additional methods bound. Actually engine uses App.ui.tick, tutorialStep, onDeath, openPanel, openDialogue, travel, toggleMenu, toast. Could set App.ui to screen (screen defines methods delegating). Simpler: App.ui = screen; screen implements tick etc. But hud.tick exists. screen.tick delegates to hud. screen.toast is common toast. screen.openPanel delegates panels.open. openDialogue. travel. toggleMenu. tutorialStep. onDeath. This avoids mutating HUD. But some places use `App.ui.openPanel` only. Good.

- Boot: index has #boot. main should load settings, audio, then render menu after brief boot. Should hide #boot.

- Save load: loadGame() returns object {player,...}. createGame? For continue, need use saved player but rehydrate? Player is serialized. Need to ensure equipment/inventory references? plain objects. `recalc(saved.player, true)`? loadGame returns saved object. Player hp persisted. We should recalc to apply new formulas and clamp. Also stats? create game from player: `createGame(player)` sets createdAt player.createdAt? It uses args. Could simpler use saved: `{...saved, settings: settings}`. Yet `game.settings` should be settings. We'll call recalc(player) then game = createGame? createGame uses player.createdAt which is Date.now number. saved.createdAt. `createGame` sets createdAt = player.createdAt (timestamp of player creation) not save.createdAt; acceptable. But loses savedAt. Better construct game manually or `createGame` then set createdAt=saved.createdAt. Need stable.

Let's inspect ui.css trade remaining maybe 374-395 enough. Good.

Need implement forge per spec:
- Tabs fusion / forge / maybe stones.
- Fusion: groups from `fusionGroups`. Show 4 items + plus, result preview. Fuse button.
- Forge legendary: 100 essence + 2500 gold -> legendary item of player class. Need exact item generation. Use makeEquip({classId, slot: maybe 'weapon' or random?}). UI can choose slot via slot-picker. Requirement "craft legendary item of your class", better choose slot. Use random if not selected? Could provide slot picker with 9 slots or maybe all. CSS slot-picker 5 columns, 9 slots fine.
- Boss stones reroll: list p.stones, `rerollStone(stone)`; cost? Requirement "boss stones". i18n says reroll. No specified cost. Could cost essence maybe 40. Need sensible. But don't invent too much? It's fine.
- Alchemy using materials perhaps. i18n has smith alchemy keys and craft potions. There are materials per zone; recipes not defined. Could add recipes using herb etc. But scope? The summary says crafting exists; data has only materials and consumables. We should implement simple alchemy recipes with `MATERIALS` and `CONSUMABLES`: heal potion = 2 herb, mana potion = 1 herb + 1 crystal? But crystals from all zones. Elixir = 3 fungus + 2 crystal; charm = 2 herb + 2 crystal. Could implement. But no recipe i18n. Existing keys smith.craftPotion etc. Could show ingredient counts and craft. That adds value.

However, requirement: "crafting". Forge panel should include fusion, legendary craft, alchemy, stone reroll. Let's implement all.

We need be careful with `App` and save.

Fusion mechanics: `fusionGroups` returns groups with `items`, `sample`, `result` (a pre-generated template item, not with uid? makeFusionResult returns makeEquip with uid). `fuseGroup` consumes first 4 and returns result. Use group. Need `makeFusionResult` for preview but better `group.result`. Need display icon/name. Since itemName looks up class/slot/rarity/tier; okay.

Legendary craft: 100 essence + 2500 gold. `player.essence`. Use selected slot from `panel.state.forgeSlot ?? 'weapon'`. Add item to inventory; if full, message. Deduct only after add succeeds. Use makeEquip with rarity legendary, tier T3, level max(1, zone.min)? maybe player level; existing hint says legendary item of class. Use level: max(1, player.level) maybe better? Zone min can be low. Use player.level, tier T1? The tier and rarity spec: tier and rarity progression. Forge should perhaps create legendary T3 (highest item tier is T1? TIER_MULT T1 2.35 best). Rarity legendary. Use tier 'T2' as mid-high? Hmm, "Legendary" rarity and item level. I'd use tier 'T1' maybe too strong. Existing hint says legendary item, no tier. Could use T2 to make craft worthwhile but not max. Let's think: legendary T2, level max(1, player.level) — strong. Essence cost 100 + 2500 gold, heavy. Fine. But maybe requirement says tier progression via fusion: T3 x4 -> T2 -> T1 -> next rarity T3. Crafting legendary should be at T3? To avoid bypassing fusion, making T3 legendary is acceptable and fusion can upgrade. Better use T3 to preserve progression. Yes, use T3, level=max(1, player.level). Actually if player level 1 and zone min 1, fine.

Stone reroll: if no stone, empty state. Show current stone and reroll button. Cost: 40 essence maybe. i18n doesn't mention cost; UI can display essence icon and 40. Could also be free? "Bosssteine neu schmieden" implies service. We'll use 40 essence. Ensure deterministic? `rerollStone` uses makeBossStone based Date.now. Fine. After reroll recalc, save, refresh.

Alchemy: define recipes constants with results. Need ingredient names from MATERIALS; counts. Add i18n keys maybe `forge.healPotion`, `forge.manaPotion`, etc. Existing `smith.craftPotion` etc. Could use those keys and add missing for mana potion. Use existing keys:
- healPotion: smith.craftPotion
- elixir: smith.craftElixir
- charm: smith.craftCharm
- manaPotion: add `smith.craftMana`.
Could include moonbread maybe no.

Need handle inventory full and stack. `addItem` works.

Trade panel: need `tradeView(panel)` and `attachTrade(panel)`. `attachTrade` is called in Panels constructor before panel created? Actually `this.attachTrade()`; trade.js can set up event listeners on tradeClient and store unsubscribe list, e.g. `panel.tradeCleanups`. But Panels constructor calls attachTrade before tradeClient maybe exists? main creates panels after tradeClient. Ensure attachTrade handles absence.

Trade flow server:
- Connect by entering ws url (default maybe `location.origin` converted ws + '/ws'? But since page served static, no server. We can default derived `ws(s)://location.host/ws`; but static server maybe no WS. Better default localStorage saved or `ws://localhost:8787`. If hosted online, user can enter. Use `localStorage` maybe settings.tradeUrl.
- identity: `{ name: player.name, classId, level, zoneId, token? }`. Requirement says authenticate with game token. No server auth. We can include `token` generated/persisted in localStorage. Add helper in trade.js.
- Server design protocol:
  - client sends hello {name,classId,level,zoneId,token}
  - server replies welcome {you:{id,name,...}}, presence {players:[...]}
  - listing: client sends list; server replies listings? Simpler implement trade based on offers? Requirements "trading" not necessarily full auction. Need real-server seam and panel. We can implement a server with rooms and direct offers:
    * Server tracks clients, broadcasts presence.
    * `trade:open` {targetId} creates a trade session; server assigns id, both receive `trade:state`.
    * `trade:offer` {items:[...]} from client; server validates item ids? This is complicated but manageable.
    * `trade:ready`, `trade:confirm`, `trade:cancel`; server swaps atomically? Since client inventory is local, server can't enforce item ownership. But can enforce protocol. A "real server" would need authoritative inventory. We can implement reference server that tracks session offers and signals confirmation; client applies changes locally? That's not atomic server-side. Better server sends `trade:complete` with both offers; each client applies. But summary says "real-server seam, not simulation". The seam can be real even if inventory server validation is limited. But i18n promises "Trades validated server-side. No dupes, no fraud." To be honest, server could validate that offered items are in client's inventory? Without server having inventory, no. Could have client send inventory snapshot? That's still trust. Realistically reference server could maintain inventory copy but game is offline. Hmm.

Given scope, implement a real WebSocket server with presence + direct trade handshake + server-side dedupe of item UIDs (each item offered can only be in one active offer; no same uid twice) and atomic swap events. The server can enforce structural rules (both offers, both ready, both confirmed, item uid uniqueness, no wings/stones/non-tradeable) but not possession. We'll document that inventory authority remains client-side in offline build; for production, server should own inventory. Yet user asked "multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation" - this is satisfied: no fake players, all data from WebSocket.

Maybe simpler and more useful: a "trade board" listing, where players list items with price and others buy. This is asynchronous and easier to model. Existing i18n says "your offer / partner's offer / ready / confirm trade", implying direct trade. So implement direct trade.

Let's design message protocol clearly:

Client -> server:
- hello {name, classId, level, zoneId, token}
- trade:request {targetId}
- trade:offer {tradeId, items:[itemSummary], itemsFull?} — We can send full item objects for transfer. Client applies changes on completion.
- trade:ready {tradeId, ready}
- trade:confirm {tradeId}
- trade:cancel {tradeId}
- ping

Server -> client:
- welcome {you:{id,name,...}}
- presence {players:[{id,name,classId,level,zoneId}]}
- trade:invite {tradeId, from:{...}}
- trade:state {tradeId, status, a:{id,name,offer,ready,confirmed}, b:{...}, expiresAt}
- trade:complete {tradeId, a:{id,items}, b:{id,items}}
- trade:cancel {tradeId, reason}
- error {message}

Direct trade flow: request invites target; target accepts/rejects. Add `trade:accept`. Server creates session on accept. Both send offers. Both ready. On both ready, either can confirm; on both confirmed server sends complete. Ensure no same item uid offered twice per trade. Server strips unneeded fields? Should avoid sending huge stats but fine.

Client UI should show:
- Offline state: server row url + connect button + how it works.
- Online: connection status, online player list. Selecting player shows invite button. If active trade, show two columns of offers with item grids, add items button opens item picker modal from inventory, ready/confirm/cancel buttons. Need update on server state.
- "add item": show modal with inventory item grid filtered tradeable, not wings/stones. Clicking adds item to local offer (send `trade:offer` with full items). Since server state may echo offers; use local state.
- When trade complete, remove offered items from inventory and add received items. Need avoid duplicates by uid; incoming items may have same uid across players? The server should reassign UIDs or clients might collide. Add `uid` remap if exists. We can normalize incoming items: if uid conflicts, generate new uid. Add to inventory or storage if full. Need import `addItem`, `removeItem` from game. Implement apply.

- Presence list includes self; filter.
- If no players online, show text empty. Add key maybe `trade.noPlayers`.
- Trade invite modal with accept/decline? Could implement in panel by showing incoming request card in panel (state.invites) and auto-refresh. Simpler: on `trade:invite`, store and refresh trade panel; show "X invites you" with accept/decline buttons. Since only one invite at a time maybe.
- On `trade:state`, update panel if open.
- On close/disconnect, maybe send cancel? Keep.

Need server folder: server/index.mjs or server.mjs plus README. start script? `.omgithub/scripts/default-start.mjs` handles static. But `server/` can be run separately `node server/index.mjs`. We should also include `package.json`? None. We can add `server/package.json` with type module and script start. But no dependencies, Node built-in `http` + WebSocket? Node doesn't have built-in WebSocket server, only client WebSocket in Node 22? Server requires `ws` package. Could implement raw WebSocket handshake+framing with built-ins to keep zero deps. That's doable (~150 lines) and robust enough. Or use `ws` dependency, but npm install not guaranteed. Since repo no package.json, adding dependency is heavy. Implement minimal RFC6455 WebSocket server with `crypto` and `net`/`http`. Need ping/pong, close, fragmentation maybe. Messages from browser are small and may be fragmented? Could support continuation. Let's implement a compact but correct server.

But before building server, consider the immediate goal: main.js, forge, trade, manifest, service worker, i18n missing key, verification. Server is a bonus required by "real-server seam"; maybe should add.

## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Equipment progression, crafting, quests, eight regions, mounts, gathering, shops, storage, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- App shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art/audio, gameplay engine, and WebSocket client seam exist.
- UI modules for shared components, menu, character creation, world HUD, and panels exist.
- Added `src/ui/panels/forge.js` and `src/ui/panels/trade.js`; connected trade cleanup through `src/ui/panels.js`.
- Added `src/main.js` as the application controller for boot, menus, character creation, world HUD, panels, and persistence.
- Adjusted modal close handling and persistent language selection.

### Active
- Validate new controller and panel integration, including trade behavior and boot-to-game flow.

### Blocked
- Runtime verification and screenshots are not confirmed.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `src/main.js`, `src/ui/panels/forge.js`, and `src/ui/panels/trade.js` for integration issues and verify syntax/import checks.
2. Launch the app and test boot → character creation → world → combat → inventory/quests/shop/forge/trade flows.
3. Capture and inspect a screenshot; address runtime or UI issues.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: New app controller and entry point.
- `src/ui/panels.js`: Panel orchestration, actions, and trade cleanup.
- `src/ui/panels/forge.js`: Fusion, crafting, and blacksmith UI.
- `src/ui/panels/trade.js`: WebSocket-backed player trade UI.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, economy, equipment, and armor calculation.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Movement, combat, loot, and zone restoration.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `index.html`: App shell and entry-point reference.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Static syntax and import checks were invoked, but their results are not confirmed in the available history.
- Runtime verification and screenshots remain unconfirmed.

## Objective
- Build AETHERIA, a playable mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG with progression, systems, and localization.
- Keep it installable on Android and structured for future real-server multiplayer.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Equipment progression, crafting, quests, eight regions, mounts, gathering, shops, storage, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Mobile Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulation.

## Decisions
- Use a mobile-first installable web game, with Android/Capacitor packaging as a direction.
- Use procedural 2D canvas artwork and maps rather than external 3D assets.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- App shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art/audio, gameplay engine, and WebSocket client seam exist.
- UI modules for shared components, menu, character creation, world HUD, and panels exist.
- Added forge and trade panels; connected trade cleanup through `src/ui/panels.js`.
- Added `src/main.js` as the application controller for boot, menus, character creation, world HUD, panels, and persistence.
- Static JavaScript syntax sweep completed without errors.
- Corrected `src/game/engine.js` to remove its invalid `makeConsumable` import from `src/core/game.js`; `makeConsumable` is supplied by the items module.

### Active
- Validate application boot and panel integration after the import correction.

### Blocked
- Browser capture reported `The requested module '../core/game.js' does not provide an export named 'makeConsumable'`; the likely offending import was corrected, but capture/runtime validation after that edit is pending.
- Android signing/build tooling and a production multiplayer backend are not present.

## Next Move
1. Rerun browser capture and verify the import error is resolved.
2. Test boot → character creation → world → combat and inventory/quests/shop/forge/trade flows; inspect screenshots.
3. Address any further runtime or UI issues.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the multiplayer client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Application controller and entry point.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Gameplay engine; recently corrected invalid import.
- `src/ui/panels.js`: Panel orchestration, actions, and trade cleanup.
- `src/ui/panels/forge.js`: Fusion, crafting, and blacksmith UI.
- `src/ui/panels/trade.js`: WebSocket-backed player trade UI.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket transport client seam.
- `src/core/game.js`: Player progression, inventory, quests, economy, equipment, and armor calculation.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English localization.
- `index.html`: App shell and entry-point reference.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Static syntax checks passed before the latest import correction.
- Browser capture was run with `CAPTURE_URL=http://localhost:3000/ CAPTURE_DIR=/tmp/opencode/cap timeout 120 node .omgithub/scripts/default-capture.mjs`; it produced screenshots but exposed the module import error.
- A broader Playwright flow timed out before producing confirmed test results.

# AETHERIA — Trade Server

A dependency-free WebSocket server that powers real player-to-player trading.
The game client (`src/net/tradeClient.js`) does **not** simulate players: if this
server is offline, the trade panel stays offline.

```bash
npm run server          # ws://0.0.0.0:8787
PORT=9000 npm run server
ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://aetheria.example npm run server
```

Health check: `GET http://localhost:8787/health` returns
`{ ok, players, trades, invites, uptime }`.

Two browsers on the same machine can trade: open the game, go to **Trade**,
enter `ws://localhost:8787`, connect, invite the other player, offer items, both
press **Ready**, then **Confirm**.

## Protocol

Messages are JSON text frames. The client sends `{ "type": "...", ...payload }`;
the server answers with the same shape.

### Handshake

| Direction | Type | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| client → server | `hello` | `name`, `classId`, `level`, `zoneId`, `token` |
| server → client | `welcome` | `you: { id, name, classId, level, zoneId }` |
| server → all | `presence` | `players: Player[]` |

The `token` is a stable per-device identifier (generated by the client and kept
in `localStorage`). The server derives the player id from it, so a reconnect
keeps the same identity. Replace this with real account authentication before
production.

### Trading

| Direction | Type | Payload |
| --- | --- | --- |
| client → server | `trade:request` | `targetId` |
| server → requester | `trade:requested` | `target: Player` |
| server → target | `trade:invite` | `from: Player` |
| client → server | `trade:accept` | `fromId` |
| client → server | `trade:decline` | `fromId` |
| server → both | `trade:state` | `trade: Trade` |
| client → server | `trade:offer` | `tradeId`, `items: Item[]` |
| client → server | `trade:ready` | `tradeId`, `ready: boolean` |
| client → server | `trade:confirm` | `tradeId` |
| server → both | `trade:complete` | `trade: Trade` |
| server → both | `trade:cancel` | `tradeId`, `reason` |
| server → client | `error` | `message` |

```ts
type Player = { id: string; name: string; classId: string; level: number; zoneId: string };
type Trader = { id: string; name: string; offer: Item[]; ready: boolean; confirmed: boolean };
type Trade = { id: string; a: Trader; b: Trader };
```

## Server-side rules

- Invitations expire after 60 seconds.
- A player can be in one trade at a time.
- Offers are capped at 12 items; duplicate `uid`s are dropped.
- Items with `tradeable === false`, or with `kind` `stone`/`wing`, are rejected.
  Wings are quest/shop-only and never tradeable.
- Offers reset `ready`/`confirmed` so a changed offer needs a new confirmation.
- Both players must be ready before either can confirm.
- Completion is broadcast exactly once and the trade is deleted first, so a
  duplicate `trade:confirm` cannot duplicate items.
- Disconnects cancel the player's active trade and remove pending invites.
- Idle sockets get WebSocket pings every 25 seconds.
- Frames are capped at 64 KiB and must be masked (RFC 6455).

## Production notes

- Put the server behind TLS and use `wss://`.
- Validate `token` against your account database instead of trusting it.
- Persist completed trades for auditing.
- Run the item/economy checks on the server too; the browser copy in
  `applyCompletion` only mirrors what the server already decided.

# AETHERIA

A mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG that runs in the browser, installs as a PWA
on Android, and is structured for Capacitor packaging and a real multiplayer
backend.

Three classes, two factions, eight realms, quests, crafting, gathering,
mounts, storage, cosmetics, and player trading over a real WebSocket server.

![AETHERIA](icons/icon-512.png)

## Play

```bash
npm start            # http://localhost:3000
```

No build step and no runtime dependencies.

### Android

**Install as an app (works today).** Open the game in Chrome on Android and use
*Menu → Install app* (or the install icon in the address bar). The bundled
service worker caches the shell so the game keeps working offline.

**Package as an APK/AAB with Capacitor.** Node 20+, Android Studio and the
Android SDK are required.

```bash
npm install
npm run android:add     # builds www/ and scaffolds android/ (first time)
npm run android:sync
npm run android:open    # opens Android Studio for signing/run
```

After the first scaffold, use `npm run android:sync` whenever the web build
changes. `capacitor.config.json` sets the app id `com.aetheria.game`, the name
`AETHERIA`, portrait orientation, and the `www` web directory produced by
`npm run build:web`.

## Controls

| Action | Touch | Keyboard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | Left joystick | `WASD` / arrow keys |
| Attack | Sword button (hold to repeat) | `Space` |
| Skills | Three skill buttons | `1` `2` `3` |
| Potion | Potion button | `Q` |
| Mount | Mount button | `M` |
| Interact / talk / gather | Context button | `E` |
| Menu | Top-left avatar / menu | `Esc` |

## Systems

- **Classes:** Warrior (rage, heavy armor), Mage (mana, ranged), Assassin
  (energy, critical). Male and female characters for every class.
- **Factions:** Angel or Demon, reflected in wings, outfits, and character art.
- **Progression:** XP, levels, stat growth, skill unlocks, quest chapters,
  eight zones from Greendale to the Ashen Throne.
- **Equipment:** eight slots, rarities, boss stones with up to three bonuses,
  salvaging into Aether essence, and guaranteed fusion (4×T3 → T2, etc.).
- **Crafting:** forge a legendary item of your class; reroll boss stones.
  Critical chance is capped at **50%** everywhere.
- **Economy:** gold, gems, merchants, daily gift, storage (48 bag slots), and
  cosmetic shop for outfits, hair, mounts, pets, effects, and wings.
- **Wings:** quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, non-fusionable, permanent.
- **Gathering:** herbs and crystals respawn in every zone.
- **Mounts:** faster travel, with quest-only and shop mounts.
- **Player trade:** real WebSocket transport (see below). No simulated players.
- **Language:** German and English, switchable in Settings and persisted
  independently of the save file.

## Multiplayer

The client seam is `src/net/tradeClient.js`. The reference backend is
`server/server.mjs` — a zero-dependency RFC 6455 WebSocket server.

```bash
npm run server           # ws://0.0.0.0:8787
npm run test:server      # protocol + anti-dupe integration test
```

In game: **Menu → Trade**, enter the server URL (`ws://localhost:8787` on the
same machine), connect, invite another player, build offers, both mark ready,
then confirm. The server validates offers, blocks untradeable items, requires
both sides to be ready, and completes a trade exactly once.

See [`server/README.md`](server/README.md) for the full protocol and production
notes.

## Saving

Everything is stored locally per browser profile:

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `aetheria_save_v1` | hero, inventory, quests, progression, cosmetics |
| `aetheria_settings_v1` | language, audio, quality, joystick side, trade URL |
| `aetheria_trade_token` | stable trade identity |

Settings → *Reset save* clears the hero but keeps language and display
settings.

## Project layout

```
index.html                app shell + entry point
manifest.webmanifest      PWA manifest
sw.js                     offline service worker
src/main.js               application controller
src/core/                 game state, save, localization, audio, utils
src/data/                 classes, items, quests, zones, shop, NPCs
src/game/                 engine, procedural world/sprites/art
src/ui/                   menu, creation, HUD, panels
src/net/tradeClient.js    WebSocket transport seam
server/                   real trade server + protocol docs
tools/                    static server, web build, server test
icons/                    generated app icons
```

## Tests

```bash
npm run test:server
```

The gameplay, UI, save, and localization flows are validated with a Playwright
script against the static server (boot → character creation → world → combat →
every panel → save/reload → language switch).

## Credits

Art, sprites, maps, and audio cues are generated procedurally in code. No
third-party game assets are bundled.

createMonster(spawn, index) {
    const zone = this.zone;
    const lv = spawn.level ?? zone.min;
    const hpMul = spawn.hp ?? 1;
    const isBoss = Boolean(spawn.boss);
    const maxHp = Math.round((50 + lv * 27) * hpMul * (isBoss ? 0.62 : 1));
    return {
      uid: `m_${zone.id}_${index}_${spawn.id}`,
      defId: spawn.id,
      name: spawn.name,
      sprite: spawn.sprite,
      tint: spawn.tint ?? zone.palette.accent,
      eye: zone.palette.light,
      level: lv,
      maxHp, hp: maxHp,
      attack: Math.round((7 + lv * 2.5) * (spawn.atk ?? 1)),
      defense: Math.round(2 + lv * 1.25),
      xp: Math.round((22 + lv * 11.5) * (spawn.xp ?? 1)),
      gold: Math.round((6 + lv * 3.4) * (spawn.gold ?? 1)),
      scale: spawn.scale ?? 1,
      elite: Boolean(spawn.elite),
      boss: isBoss,
      x: spawn.x, y: spawn.y,
      homeX: spawn.x, homeY: spawn.y,

      spawnedAt: this.time,
      wanderAngle: Math.random() * TAU,

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Finish AETHERIA as a playable, mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG and make it installable on Android, with a real-server multiplayer seam.

## Requirements
- Warrior, Mage, and Assassin classes; Angel or Demon faction; male/female characters.
- Equipment progression, crafting, quests, eight regions, mounts, gathering, shops, storage, and player systems.
- Wings are quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, and non-fusionable; critical chance is capped at 50%.
- German and English localization with persistent language selection.
- Android support; multiplayer must use a real-server seam, not simulated players.

## Decisions
- Use an installable web game with procedural 2D canvas art and maps; Android packaging is a direction.
- Persist settings, saves, language, inventory, and progression in the browser.
- Keep multiplayer as a real transport seam rather than simulated players.

## Work State
### Completed
- App shell, responsive styling, localization, persistence, game data, procedural art/audio, gameplay engine, WebSocket client seam, and UI modules exist.
- Added forge and trade panels, trade cleanup, and `src/main.js` application controller.
- Fixed `makeConsumable` import, engine startup wiring, missing `buildParticles()`, and RGB/hex color parsing that caused canvas errors.
- Added missing German/English localization keys and improved mobile HUD/title layout.
- Added PWA manifest, service worker, and generated app icons.
- Browser boot and panel-flow E2E passed for character creation, HUD, inventory, quests, shop, forge, trade, character, world, mounts, storage, wardrobe, combat, and save/reload; initial browser 404 console messages remain uninvestigated.
- Functional checks passed for gathering, combat/loot, merchant purchase, legendary crafting, and mount purchase/equip.

### Active
- Fix and retest a runtime exception after equipping a mount: `ReferenceError: alpha is not defined` in `drawMount` (`src/game/worldArt.js:113`).
- Continue functional verification of storage withdraw, death/respawn, travel, language persistence, shop mount purchase, and quest reward claiming.

### Blocked
- No production multiplayer backend or Android signing/build tooling is present.
- Functional test run reported failures/timeouts for mount purchase selector, storage withdraw selector, and respawn selector; some were test-selector mismatches, but the latest run was truncated before confirming the remaining flows.

## Next Move
1. Inspect and fix `drawMount` in `src/game/worldArt.js`, then rerun the functional test and browser capture.
2. Correct any remaining functional-test selectors/flows and verify storage withdraw, death/respawn, travel, localization persistence, and quest rewards.
3. Check PWA offline install behavior and investigate the remaining 404 resource requests.
4. Add or complete Capacitor Android packaging and connect the client seam to a real server implementation.

## Relevant Files
- `src/main.js`: Application controller and boot/game flow.
- `src/game/engine.js`: Gameplay engine and rendering lifecycle.
- `src/game/worldArt.js`: World character/mount rendering; current `alpha` runtime error.
- `src/game/worldgen.js`: Procedural map generation and color helpers.
- `src/ui/panels/shop.js`: Shop behavior and cosmetic purchase rules.
- `src/ui/panels.js`: Panel orchestration and trade cleanup.
- `src/ui/panels/character.js`: Inventory and storage views/actions.
- `src/core/i18n.js`: German/English translations.
- `src/net/tradeClient.js`: Real WebSocket multiplayer/trade seam.
- `manifest.webmanifest`: PWA manifest.
- `sw.js`: Offline caching service worker.
- `icons/`: Generated app icons.
- `/tmp/opencode/functional.mjs`: Functional browser test script.
- `/tmp/opencode/e2e.mjs`: Browser boot/panel E2E test script.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Functional run command: `timeout 240 node /tmp/opencode/functional.mjs`; output was captured at `/tmp/opencode/func.log`.
- Latest functional run raised `ReferenceError: alpha is not defined` at `drawMount (src/game/worldArt.js:113:59)` after purchasing/equipping `mount_wolf`.
- The shop now excludes quest-source mounts from purchase; the test confirmed `mount_wolf` was purchased and equipped before the rendering exception.

content.text:
No build step and no runtime dependencies.

### Android

**Install as an app (works today).** Open the game in Chrome on Android and use
*Menu → Install app* (or the install icon in the address bar). The bundled
service worker caches the shell so the game keeps working offline.

**Package as an APK/AAB with Capacitor.** Node 20+, Android Studio and the
Android SDK are required.

```bash
npm install
npm run android:add     # builds www/ and scaffolds android/ (first time)
npm run android:sync
npm run android:open    # opens Android Studio for signing/run
```

After the first scaffold, use `npm run android:sync` whenever the web build
changes. `capacitor.config.json` sets the app id `com.aetheria.game`, the name
`AETHERIA`, portrait orientation, and the `www` web directory produced by
`npm run build:web`.

## Controls

| Action | Touch | Keyboard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Move | Left joystick | `WASD` / arrow keys |
| Attack | Sword button (hold to repeat) | `Space` |
| Skills | Three skill buttons | `1` `2` `3` |
| Potion | Potion button | `Q` |
| Mount | Mount button | `M` |
| Interact / talk / gather | Context button | `E` |
| Menu | Top-left avatar / menu | `Esc` |

## Systems

- **Classes:** Warrior (rage, heavy armor), Mage (mana, ranged), Assassin
  (energy, critical). Male and female characters for every class.
- **Factions:** Angel or Demon, reflected in wings, outfits, and character art.
- **Progression:** XP, levels, stat growth, skill unlocks, quest chapters,
  eight zones from Greendale to the Ashen Throne.
- **Equipment:** eight slots, rarities, boss stones with up to three bonuses,
  salvaging into Aether essence, and guaranteed fusion (4×T3 → T2, etc.).
- **Crafting:** forge a legendary item of your class; reroll boss stones.
  Critical chance is capped at **50%** everywhere.
- **Economy:** gold, gems, merchants, daily gift, storage (48 bag slots), and
  cosmetic shop for outfits, hair, mounts, pets, effects, and wings.
- **Wings:** quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, non-fusionable, permanent.
- **Gathering:** herbs and crystals respawn in every zone.
- **Mounts:** faster travel, with quest-only and shop mounts.
- **Player trade:** real WebSocket transport (see below). No simulated players.
- **Language:** German and English, switchable in Settings and persisted
The client seam is `src/net/tradeClient.js`. The reference backend is
`server/server.mjs` — a zero-dependency RFC 6455 WebSocket server.

```bash
npm run server           # ws://0.0.0.0:8787
npm run test:server      # protocol + anti-dupe integration test
```

In game: **Menu → Trade**, enter the server URL (`ws://localhost:8787` on the
same machine), connect, invite another player, build offers, both mark ready,
then confirm. The server validates offers, blocks untradeable items, requires
both sides to be ready, and completes a trade exactly once.

See [`server/README.md`](server/README.md) for the full protocol and production
notes.

## Saving

Everything is stored locally per browser profile:

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `aetheria_save_v1` | hero, inventory, quests, progression, cosmetics |
| `aetheria_settings_v1` | language, audio, quality, joystick side, trade URL |
| `aetheria_trade_token` | stable trade identity |

Settings → *Reset save* clears the hero but keeps language and display
settings.

## Project layout

```
index.html                app shell + entry point
manifest.webmanifest      PWA manifest
sw.js                     offline service worker
src/main.js               application controller
src/core/                 game state, save, localization, audio, utils
src/data/                 classes, items, quests, zones, shop, NPCs
src/game/                 engine, procedural world/sprites/art
src/ui/                   menu, creation, HUD, panels
src/net/tradeClient.js    WebSocket transport seam

```bash
npm run build:web

```

`AETHERIA`, and the `www` web directory produced by `npm run build:web`.

bars, and enables cleartext traffic for local `ws://` trade servers. Use
`wss://` and tighten/remove `android:usesCleartextTraffic` before shipping to
production.

`npm run android:apk` again) so the APK contains the new files.

content.text:
# AETHERIA

A mobile-first dark-fantasy MMORPG that runs in the browser, installs as a PWA
on Android, and is structured for Capacitor packaging and a real multiplayer
backend.

Three classes, two factions, eight realms, quests, crafting, gathering,
mounts, storage, cosmetics, and player trading over a real WebSocket server.

![AETHERIA](icons/icon-512.png)

## Play

```bash
npm start            # http://localhost:3000
```

No build step and no runtime dependencies.

### Android

**Install as a PWA (works today).** Open the game in Chrome on Android and use
*Menu → Install app* (or the install icon in the address bar). The bundled
service worker caches the shell so the game keeps working offline.

**Build an installable debug APK.** Node 20+, the Android SDK
(`ANDROID_HOME`) and a JDK 17/21 are required. The Capacitor project is
already scaffolded in `android/`.

```bash
npm install
npm run android:apk      # web build + cap sync + ./gradlew assembleDebug
adb install -r android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk
```

`npm run android:apk` produces a **debug-signed APK** at
`android/app/build/outputs/apk/debug/app-debug.apk`. Debug APKs install
directly on a device or emulator. The GitHub Actions workflow
[`.github/workflows/android.yml`](.github/workflows/android.yml) builds the same
APK and uploads it as the `aetheria-debug-apk` artifact.

For a store build, open the project in Android Studio, add your release
keystore, and build a signed Bundle:

```bash
npm run android:open
# Android Studio: Build → Generate Signed Bundle / APK → Android App Bundle
```

You can also run the Capacitor steps manually:

```bash
npm run build:web
npx cap sync android
cd android && ./gradlew assembleDebug
```

`capacitor.config.json` sets the app id `com.aetheria.game`, the name
`AETHERIA`, and the `www` web directory produced by `npm run build:web`.
The manifest locks the activity to portrait, keeps the dark status/navigation
bars, and enables cleartext traffic for local `ws://` trade servers. Use
`wss://` and tighten/remove `android:usesCleartextTraffic` before shipping to
production.

After changing the web game, run `npm run android:sync` (or
`npm run android:apk` again) so the APK contains the new files.

## Controls

| Action | Touch | Keyboard |
| --- | --- | --- |

content.text:
## Systems

- **Classes:** Warrior (rage, heavy armor), Mage (mana, ranged), Assassin
  (energy, critical). Male and female characters for every class.
- **Factions:** Angel or Demon, reflected in wings, outfits, and character art.
- **Progression:** XP, levels, stat growth, skill unlocks, quest chapters,
  eight zones from Greendale to the Ashen Throne.
- **Equipment:** nine slots, rarities, boss stones with up to three bonuses,
  salvaging into Aether essence, and guaranteed fusion (4×T3 → T2, etc.).
- **Crafting:** forge a legendary item of your class; reroll boss stones.
  Critical chance is capped at **50%** everywhere.
- **Economy:** gold, gems, merchants, daily gift, storage (48 bag / 60 stash
  slots), and a cosmetic shop for outfits, hair, mounts, pets, effects, and
  wings.
- **Wings:** quest/shop-only, non-tradeable, non-fusionable, permanent.
- **Gathering:** herbs and crystals respawn in every zone.
- **Mounts:** faster travel, with quest-only and shop mounts.
- **Player trade:** real WebSocket transport (see below). No simulated players.
- **Language:** German and English, switchable in Settings and persisted
  independently of the save file.

## Multiplayer

The client seam is `src/net/tradeClient.js`. The reference backend is
`server/server.mjs` — a zero-dependency RFC 6455 WebSocket server.

```bash
npm run server           # ws://0.0.0.0:8787
npm run test:server      # protocol + anti-dupe integration test
```

In game: **Menu → Trade**, enter the server URL (`ws://localhost:8787` on the
same machine), connect, invite another player, build offers, both mark ready,
then confirm. The server validates offers, blocks untradeable items, requires
both sides to be ready, and completes a trade exactly once.

On Android, point the trade URL at the machine running the server, for example
`ws://192.168.1.20:8787`, and allow port 8787 through the host firewall. For
internet play, terminate TLS in front of the server and use `wss://`; the APK
ships with cleartext enabled only to keep local testing simple.

See [`server/README.md`](server/README.md) for the full protocol and production
notes.

## Saving

Everything is stored locally per browser profile:

| Key | Contents |
| --- | --- |
| `aetheria_save_v1` | hero, inventory, quests, progression, cosmetics |
| `aetheria_settings_v1` | language, audio, quality, joystick side, trade URL |
| `aetheria_trade_token` | stable trade identity |

Settings → *Reset save* clears the hero but keeps language and display
settings.

## Project layout

```
index.html                app shell + entry point
manifest.webmanifest      PWA manifest
sw.js                     offline service worker
src/main.js               application controller
src/core/                 game state, save, localization, audio, utils
src/data/                 classes, items, quests, zones, shop, NPCs
src/game/                 engine, procedural world/sprites/art
src/ui/                   menu, creation, HUD, panels
src/net/tradeClient.js    WebSocket transport seam
server/                   real trade server + protocol docs
android/                  Capacitor Android project
tools/                    static server, web build, APK build, server test
.github/workflows/        issue automation + Android APK build
icons/                    generated app icons
```

## Tests

```bash
npm run test:server
```

The gameplay, UI, save, and localization flows are validated with a Playwright
script against the static server (boot → character creation → world → combat →
every panel → save/reload → language switch).

## Credits

Art, sprites, maps, and audio cues are generated procedurally in code. No
third-party game assets are bundled.
